To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the gluino is harder to detect in certain channels in $E_8$ inspired models, but that it can be more easily detected in other channels.
gluino decays in $SU(5)$ inspired models are distinguishable from the Minimal Supersymmetic Standard Model (MMSM) in 3- and possibly 4-lepton channels.
$E_8$ inspired models have a distinctive gluino signature in 3-lepton channels, and that the gluino mass in these models is likely to be above 2 TeV, if it exists at all.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the phenomenology of supersymmetry in models inspired by $E_6$. In this context, we have studied the gluino cascade decaying via the extra neutralinos in $E_8 \times E_6$ inspired supersymmetry.
the study of the phenomenology of the $E_8\times E_6$ inspired model and its supersymmetric extension.
the phenomenological implications of the extended neutralino and chargino sectors of $E_ 6$ inspired models in gluino cascade decay chains, which are of particular relevance for the LHC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the gluino is easier to discover in the MSSM than in $E_7$ inspired models, but that the gluino can be discovered more easily in $E_8$ inspired models, due to the presence of a 4-lepton channel, which is absent in the MSSM and in $E_5$ inspired models.
, in general, the discovery potential of the LHC for gluinos is reduced in $E_ 6$ inspired models compared to the MSSSM, but that this can be overcome in the 3- and/or 4-lepton channels.
$E_8$ models are clearly distinguishible from MSSM in the gluino cascade decaying into the first generation of quark, but not from the MSSM models in gluino cascade into the third generation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
$E_ 6$ inspired models can lead to a more complicated gluino cascade decay, and this may lead to more visible transverse momentum, softer jets and less missing transvers energy than the MSSM.
the gluino cascade decaying into the neutralinos and chargoninos of $E_ 6$ models is more visible than that in the MSSM.

, in the context of $E_8$ inspired models, gluino cascade decaying into a pair of lightest supersymmetric particles is not necessarily the most promising channel for discovering the supersymmetric particles at the Large Hadron Collider.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the gluino cascade decaying in the $E_7$ inspired models is harder to find in the conventional channels, but can be discovered in the 3- and/or 4-lepton channels, and is clearly distinguishable from gluino decays in the MSSM.
the $E_8$ inspired models can be tested in the LHC, even if the gluino is beyond the reach of the conventional searches.

, while gluinos in the $E_8$ models can be harder to discover than the MSSM, they are more visible in the 3-leptons and 4-leptons channels, making the discovery of these models in gluino decays possible.
